title: Packet Configuration
description: Pick the interfaces to capture, save, then start. Everything else is under Advanced and has defaults that suit most captures. Live capture needs a one-time grant on the machine running the agent; run the Check permissions action first. Decoding a pcap file needs no privileges at all.

interfaces.title: Interfaces
interfaces.description: Interfaces to capture from, in parallel. They share the one 'Packet' trace source and appear side by side under it, one branch per capture. The capture settings below apply to every one of them. Leave empty when using Replay PCAP File.

interface.title: Interface
interface.description: Network interface to capture on (eth0, en0, wlan0, lo, ...). Choose from the machine running the agent, or type a name.

name.title: Name
name.description: Names this capture's branch in the signal tree. Defaults to the interface name, which is usually what you want. Dots, colons, '@' and '/' are replaced with '_' because they are catalog path separators, so a VLAN device eth0.100 becomes eth0_100. Every capture shares the one 'Packet' source, so each name must be unique.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.description: Capture and storage settings that apply to every interface. The defaults suit most captures.

snaplen.title: Snapshot Length (bytes captured)
snaplen.description: Bytes captured per packet on every interface; the rest is truncated by the kernel. This is the CAPTURE limit - what reaches the decoder at all. 512 keeps the whole embedded/industrial control plane byte-complete - every legal Modbus-TCP frame (MBAP 7 + PDU up to 253, about 314 B once Ethernet/IP/TCP headers are counted), DHCP (whose semantics live in the options after the 236-byte BOOTP area), DNS and mDNS responses, MQTT CONNECT, DoIP, SOME/IP and PTP - while cutting bulk transfers so a file copy does not fill the trace. 128 would break DHCP and DNS responses outright. Raise it only when you need full payloads. Unset, it is 512, or 1518 (a full Ethernet frame) when ARXML files or SOME/IP ports are set, so SOME/IP payloads arrive whole.

promiscuous.title: Promiscuous Mode
promiscuous.description: Capture every frame on the segment, not just frames addressed to this host, on every interface. Off by default: on a switched network it mostly adds noise, and some drivers and VM NICs lose throughput sharply in promiscuous mode. Turn it on when capturing from a mirror/SPAN port or a tap.

buffer_size.title: Kernel Buffer Size (bytes)
buffer_size.description: Kernel capture buffer, per interface. Larger buffers absorb bursts without kernel drops, at the cost of RAM. If the 'dropped' counter in the 'Capture stats' action climbs, raise this.

replay_pcap.title: Replay PCAP File
replay_pcap.description: Decode a .pcap/.pcapng file instead of capturing live. This path opens no capture handle and needs no privileges, so it works on any machine - use it to try the extension, or to analyze a capture someone sent you. Plays at the capture's original pace with timestamps shifted to start now. When set, the Interfaces list is ignored and the extension exits once the replay finishes.

log_frames.title: Log Raw Frames
log_frames.description: Populate the 'frame' Binary column with the captured bytes (up to Frame Bytes Stored). Turn it off to keep only decoded header fields, which makes traces far smaller.

stored_frame_bytes.title: Frame Bytes Stored
stored_frame_bytes.description: Bytes of each captured packet kept in the 'frame' column. This is the STORAGE limit, not a capture limit: dissection always reads every captured byte, so the decoded columns are the same whatever this is set to, and 'orig_len'/'cap_len'/'truncated' keep describing capture truncation rather than this. null (the default) stores every captured byte, so the Snapshot Length is the single byte budget and the control plane stays byte-complete in the frame column - Modbus-TCP, DHCP, DNS/mDNS. Set a number to store only a prefix and shrink traces.

arxml.title: ARXML Files
arxml.description: AUTOSAR ARXML files (R4.2 or R19-11 and later), loaded as one system. SOME/IP payloads of the services they describe decode into the 'SOMEIP' source, one event per event, method and field with one column per value. Load the ECU extract for the ECUs on the tapped link rather than a whole-vehicle file. With ARXML and no Snapshot Length set, 1518 bytes are captured per packet.

someip.title: SOME/IP
someip.description: SOME/IP messages land in '<capture>/someip', one row per message; SD entries in '<capture>/someip_sd'. Ports SD offers and the ARXML names are dissected as SOME/IP on their own.

sd_port.title: SD Port
sd_port.description: UDP port of SOME/IP Service Discovery. null turns SD off.

ports.title: More SOME/IP Ports
ports.description: SOME/IP ports, UDP or TCP, beyond those SD offers and the ARXML name.

doip.title: DoIP
doip.description: Diagnostics over IP (ISO 13400) lands in '<capture>/doip', one row per message, with the UDS service id of each diagnostic message.

port.title: DoIP Port
port.description: UDP and TCP port of DoIP. null turns DoIP off.
